detail.otherInfo:
Shri Nilesh Dnyandev Lanke knows as Covid warrior. He had started two-time world's first private covid center during Corona. In which a record breaking 33,500 people were successfully treated. Due to the various treatment methods and the measures taken to allay the fears of the patients about Covid, they became known in the country. In 2019, he was elected MLA of the Parner-Nagar Assembly constituency in Maharashtra.

Born on 10th March 1980, at a young age, he wanted a letter of recommendation from an MLA for a job, but as he did not get it, he tried many different professions but was unsuccessful. Since then, he started his social activities. Seeing his social work, many youths get influenced by him and joined him. He was elected MLA in 2019. Before that he was only elected as Gram Panchayat member.

FIRST COVID CENTRE WORK
Due to the first sudden lockdown in India in 2020 due to COVID-19, many people had to face different problems. In this, the number of poor, workers and displaced people was high. Since the second day of the lockdown, he set up a food stall on different place and distribute free meal to more than 2 lack peoples, put sandals for barefoot peoples. He distributed groceries kit for more than 5 thousand families and made arrangements to take the people of the village outside to their homes through vehicles. He provided these services for more than two consecutive months. He also started India’s first private covid center in first wave of covid-19, in Parner tehsil.  It was one thousand bed covid center and around five thousand patients, which was from different places was successfully recover from that centre.

SECOND COVID CENTRE WORK
With experience of 1st covid wave, in second wave of covid-19 in 2021, he set up a one thousand one hundred bed with hundred oxygen bed covid center. Which lasted for more than six months and treated around 29 thousand people. This Covid center had patients from different districts of Maharashtra and other states. In this covid center patients were given nutritious food, daily different cultural programs were organized in the covid center to remove their fear of covid. Some patients were treated naturally and also arranging plasma donation camp. A marriage was also organized in this Covid center. Along with the state of Maharashtra, people from different regions of the country visited here and get information.

AWARDS
Shri Nilesh Lanke has been conferred several prestigious awards. He received the international ‘Global Humanitarian Award 2022’ by the ‘Word Records Union’ for the public health. He received ‘World Book of Records London- 2021’certificate of commitments. He has also received ‘Lokmat Mharashtrian of The Year 2020’ and ‘Maharashtra Covid Yodha- 2021’. In addition, he has received several awards and honours from leading institutions, organization of Maharashtra.

detail.interest:
Experience in Energy Sector
Very few IAS officers would have the opportunity of serving in all the three wings, viz., Distribution, Transmission and Generation as Managing Director of the respective public utilities of Karnataka and also as the Additional Chief Secretary for the Department. While in BESCOM(Bangalore Electricity Distribution Company) I have strived for the implementation of Distribution Automation System (DAS) to improve control of distribution network. While in KPTCL(Karnataka Power Transmission Company Limited) I have planned and tendered out for setting up of 400 KV transmission lines from thermal stations in northern part of the State to Bangalore situated in the southern part. While in KPCL(Karnataka Power Corporation Limited, an electricity generation company)  I was able to successfully commission 2x800 MW of super critical boiler technology coal based thermal power plants at Yeramarus, Raichur augmenting much needed generation capacity. I also brought in operation and maintenance contract for this power plant resulting in the saving of approximately Rs 388 crores for the corporation. As Additional Chief Secretary I was able to put in place a robust mechanism for Energy trading in energy markets for conventional as well as green power. Over Rs 6000 Crs were earned for the State Discoms by sale of energy. I was able to bring out Karnataka Renewable Energy Policy 2022-2027 and Karnataka Energy Efficiency and Conservation Policy 2022-2027 to align the targets of the State with that of the Country. Considering my experience I was appointed to the National Level Committee to look into the 'Deviation Settlement Mechanism Regulation’. As the Chairman of Karnataka Renewable Energy Development Corporation, I was able to promote growth of solar and wind sources of energy taking Karnataka to the top-most position in the country. 
I would like to contribute towards growth of conventional as well as renewable energy sector and ensure position of India as a champion of renewable energy and provide leadership for Energy/Carbon Emission reduction negotiations at different fora across the globe.
detail.education:
B.E. (Civil Engineering)
University Visvesvaraya College of Engineering, Bangalore University
detail.otherInfo:
Education Sector 
1)	Primary Education:
To ensure 100% enrolment and retention of students many programs were implemented. Both as Commissioner and as Secretary to the Department I strived hard to ensure timely flow of funds, completion of tendering process, procurement and distribution of text books, uniforms and bicycles to each and every targeted student in every Primary and Secondary schools in the State. Mid-day Meal program was implemented in every school without interruption throughout the year. As a measure of joyful learning, ' NALI KALI ', an adaptation of Montessori system was introduced across the State in all Primary schools after ensuring training of a large number of teachers and provision of relevant learning material.
I was instrumental in strengthening the Karnataka State Quality Assessment Organization which was to comprehensively asses the Quality of Schools. Subsequently with the help of NGO's a remedial teaching program was conducted across the State.
To align Teachers Education with the National Curriculum Frame-work the syllabus was fully revamped.
For the very first time a law, The Karnataka State Civil Service (Regulation of Transfer of Teachers) was enacted for transfer of teachers which aimed at balancing availability of teachers in the schools and gaining trust of teachers in the transfer process. This measure has prevented arbitrary and frequent transfers.
As directed by the Government, I submitted a Report on the demands of Pre University Lectures who were on strike after detailed study. The report popularly referred to as “Kumar Naik Report” was widely welcomed by teaching fraternity and substantially accepted by the Government of Karnataka.
2)	Higher Education:
As Additional Chief Secretary I had the opportunity to implement New Education Policy – 2020 (NEP-2020) in Karnataka. With a clear intent we initiated,  a) Academic Reforms and b) Governance and Regulatory Reforms based on reports submitted by the Task Force for implementation of NEP 2020. Steps taken in Karnataka to ensure student centric, holistic and multi- disciplinary Undergraduate Education were emulated by different States. Assessment procedures were revised across the State. Academic reforms involved formulation of modular curriculum and introduction of Skill course through collaborations. As a part of Governance and Regulatory Reforms, 1) Karnataka Shikshana Ayoga Bill 2022 and 2) Karnataka State Higher Education Institutions Bill 2022 were framed. NEP implementation was accompanied by a slew of technological interventions. Comprehensive Learning Management System (LMS) was supported by internet enabled smart class rooms and Tablet PCs given to all Degree students. For all the Universities a common end to end ERP kind of software has been developed for the very first time in the Country. Named Unified University and College Management System (UUCMS), this software assists in performance of different functions - Admission, Class room management, Examination, Finance, Human resource management, Affiliation etc. This has been implemented across 23 State Public Universities and 3800 Affiliated Colleges with the help of Centre for Smart Governance, Dept. of E-Governance Govt. of Karnataka.

Urban Administration
I have the unique experience, rarely available to IAS officers, of heading the City Corporation (BBMP) and City Development Authority (BDA) as Commissioner. Under the official Administrator I had the opportunity to revamp many existing practices of the City Corporation. Online property Tax collection system required whole lot of preparatory work like correct enlisting of all the properties in the City, proper assessment of Tax, timely issuances of Notice and smooth payment mechanism. I strived to put a robust system in place which eliminated hardship for the citizens and increased the collection of Taxes.
I improved upon the existing system of maintaining history of road construction and maintenance which resulted in reduction in repetition of works and wasteful expenditure. Most important work I could deliver was construction of 7 solid waste processing plants and 17 Bio-methanation plants across the city. Wide publicity was given to create awareness regarding segregation of dry and wet waste at source itself. I took it upon the corporation to coordinate continuously and effectively among various civic agency like BWSSB, BESCOM, Traffic Police and BDA for ensuring timely completion of projects with minimum disruption of citizens lives and minimum wastage. As Commissioner of the Bangalore Development Authority I worked hard to complete a layout directly under the supervision of the Supreme Court appointed committee. I speeded up the long pending and lingering works of different new areas being developed by raising funds, allotting works and monitoring the execution of these works.
Welfare Administration
As Principal Secretary of Social Welfare Department I had the opportunity to implement programs directly connected with Welfare of the weakest sections of the society, the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes. For the first time The SC/ST Scheduled Caste Sub Plan and Tribunal Sub Plan Act 2013 and Rules 2017, a unique legislation in the country, was implemented in full vigour. A special cell was constituted to monitor allotment, release and utilization of funds in different Departments. I strived vigorously to ensure that the cell played an important role in safe guarding the allotted funds, in qualitatively improving the programs by efficient collection and analysis of data pertaining to implementation. Self-employment programs with three innovative business models were taken up to fuel the spirit of entrepreneurship and to create sustainable income generation opportunities. AIRAVATHA envisaged partnership with cab aggregators like Ola and Uber to facilitate employment of rural youth through radio taxi. SAMRUDDHI assisted the applicants in setting up retail outlets after having gone through rigorous training program facilitated by the Brand franchiser. UNNATI provided a comprehensive entrepreneurship platform for start-ups that have a technological and social component built into their offering. Identifying the Innovation, Validating it and providing Seed Capital uptoRs. 50 Lakhs were activities under the program. All these three programs have received positive response. I had the opportunity to efficiently run about 850 residential schools catering to 155000 children across the State, by far the largest effort among all the States in the Country. Efforts were made to develop identified residential schools into Sports Schools and Sainik Schools. Similarly 2122 hostels were run efficiently for the benefit of nearly 2 lakh hostellers belonging to the SCs and STs.

3)	Karnataka Renewable Energy Development Limited (KREDL) has won the 1stprize in the State Designated Agency (SDA Group-1) Sector at the National Energy Conservation Awards 2022 the award was presented by the Hon’ble President of India Smt. Delegations led by Smt. Anupriya Patel in her capacity as Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare
In the capacity of Hon’ble Minister of State for Health & Family Welfare, Smt. Anupriya Patel led a delegation to the Commonwealths of Dominica and Grenada from 8-17th May, 2018 under the ‘VRIHAD SAMPARK YOJANA’ of Ministry of External Affairs. It was the first Ministerial visit from India to these countries.
During her visit to Dominica from 11th to 12th May, 2018, she met the Hon’ble President, Hon’ble Prime Minister and Acting Minister of Foreign Affairs, Hon’ble Health Minister, Hon’ble Minister of Family and Gender Affairs of Dominican Republic and discussed the issues of importance between the two countries. While in Grenada during 13-14th May, 2018, she called on Shri Keith Mitchell, Hon’ble Prime Minister, Hon’ble Foreign Minister and Hon’ble Health Minister of Grenada and discussed areas of mutual interest to enhance overall cooperation between the two countries. While meeting the Hon’ble Prime Minister of Grenada, Smt. Anupriya Patel handed over a congratulatory letter from Shri Narendra Modi ji, Hon’ble Prime Minister of India.
During her visit to both the countries, the Hon’ble Minister met the Indian community and interacted with them.
Delegations led by Smt. Anupriya Patel ji in her capacity as Union Minister of State for Commerce & Industry
Greece during April 14-15, 2022:
As Hon’ble Minister of State for Commerce & Industry, Smt. Anupriya Patel led a delegation to Greece during April 14 – 15, 2022 to co-chair the 8th session of the India-Greece Joint Economic Committee meeting with Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Responsible for Economic Diplomacy and Openness, Kostas Fragkogiannis. During the meeting, a Protocol was signed by both the Ministers aimed at strengthening and further developing the economic and trade relations for mutual benefit of both the countries. A Memorandum of Understanding on Enhancing Bilateral Investment Relations between Invest India, National Investment Promotion and Facilitation Agency of India and Enterprise, Greece was also exchanged by both the Ministers.
Bangkok, Thailand during May 23-24, 2022:
Smt. Anupriya Patel led a delegation to Bangkok, Thailand during May 23-24, 2022 to attend the 78th session of the UNESCAP, which was also commemorating the 75th anniversary of its foundation. During the Ministerial segment of the 78th session of UNESCAP, the Hon’ble Minister delivered country statement on the theme, “A common agenda to advance sustainable development in Asia and the Pacific”.
Siem Reap City, Cambodia during September 16-17, 2022:
The Hon’ble Minister led another Indian delegation to Siem Reap City, Cambodia to co-chair the 19th ASEAN-India Economic Ministers’ Meeting along with H.E. Pan Sorasak, Minister of Commerce, Kingdom of Cambodia on 16th September, 2022 and to represent India in the 10th East Asia Summit Economic Ministers’ Meeting held on 17th September, 2022. The meeting saw representation from all 10 ASEAN countries as well as 8 partner countries viz. Australia, China, India, Japan, New Zealand, Republic of Korea, Russian Federation and the USA. detail.otherInfo:
Born on 28th April, 1981 at Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh, Smt. Anupriya Patel is a well known face of Indian politics. Her father, late Dr. Soney Lal Patel, was founder of Apna Dal, whose untimely demise in a road accident suddenly propelled Smt. Patel into her political journey.
She is blessed with excellent oratory skills and always speaks emphatically on the floor of the House. As a Member of Parliament, she has made a mark with her meaningful interventions in the parliamentary debates and discussions.
Her commitment and unparalleled spirit to work towards strengthening the social justice ideology is admired by people at large. She has garnered widespread public support for the developmental initiatives undertaken in her Parliamentary constituency, Mirzapur and beyond.
Smt. Anupriya Singh Patel, face of resurgence of the underprivileged, presents a strong image of a leader who is passionate, decisive and committed towards the cause of the oppressed and marginalised sections of the society. She is truly a ‘role-model’ not only for women but even for the youth in a young nation like India. She leads by setting examples and inspires people to contribute towards the nation’s progress.
At the age of 35 years, she took oath as the ‘Youngest Minister’ in Modi - 1 Government and served as Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare. She made her second start in the Council of Ministers as Minister of State for Commerce & Industry in Modi – 2 Government.

He has served as the Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development & Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Parliamentary Affairs in Shri Narendra Modi’s government. In Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee’s government, was the Minister of State for Commerce and Industry and later, the Minister of State with Independent Charge of Civil Aviation in 2003. Elected as a State Legislator from Bihar at the age of 27 in the 1990s. Served in various organizational roles, including the National General Secretary and the National Spokesperson of Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), in his political career spanning nearly three decades;

Modernisation of Indian Airports, launch of Low Cost Airlines, ATF tax reduction, abolition of IATT, revising the charter policy etc. were some major milestones. He is credited as the only Parliamentarian on globe Captaining Airbus-320 Jets, flying with one of the largest airlines in India and also figures in the Limca book of World records.
